title: "We may use Google Analytics to collect your browser information"
body:
### What is the problem?

Directly from Violentmonkey's privacy policy: "We may use Google Analytics to collect your browser information anonymously to help improve compatibility."

Why..? This is unneeded. It would be a good decision to remove this, or make it an opt-in only feature, disabled by default. This is a privacy concern. I've come across many users switching off violentmonkey simply due to this. It doesn't matter if it's anonymously collected, this is what people don't want. They don't want their data collected like this. Please, I highly encourage you to remove this.

Screenshot: https://b.catgirlsare.sexy/cTV7.png

### How to reproduce it?
1. View Privacy Policy
author: Participant 1

comments.author: Participant 2
comments.body:
Thanks for the kind suggestion.

To make it clear, I plan to collect the browser type / version and system type / version so that I can decide which browsers to support when considering new JavaScript features.

I'm wondering if my words are improper or people just don't want anything to be collected? If the latter is true, I think I can remove that plan and just drop support for old browsers in the future.

comments.author: Participant 1
comments.body:
>To make it clear, I plan to collect the browser type / version and system type / version so that I can decide which browsers to support when considering new JavaScript features.

Yes but I agree with them, I understand your reasoning but a lot of people who are privacy conscious simply want to minimize/deny data collection, and I think it's a good idea to either have it disabled by default and allow people to opt-in or the other way around, or even better just completely disable it. I genuinely think this would be a good descision.

comments.author: Participant 3
comments.body:
@Z3ROGRAV1TYx The problem is if it is **opt-in**, almost no one will turn it on. I agree that there should be a button to disable analytics, but whether it should be on or off by default is debatable.
Currently, there is no such button in Violentmonkey settings to turn off analytics , and it should be one there.

comments.body:
Mozilla has probably partially solved this with:

[blog.mozilla.org/addons/2025/10/23/data-collection-consent-changes-for-new-firefox-extensions](https://blog.mozilla.org/addons/2025/10/23/data-collection-consent-changes-for-new-firefox-extensions/)

There is no need to rush, because it will cut off Firefox 57-115.12 users (It's enough that the other group got hit with the expiration of the main/root certificate once or twice, if can't migrate to 115.13.0+), as only versions 115.31.0 RC1 and 128+ can handle marking this as a minor bug, while older versions report that the add-on is supposedly broken.

The exact release date for add-ons with a longer history than the November 3 store release will be announced in newer blog posts.
